subject: Unexpected latency spike during morning window — decision log & customer notice
messages:

FYI — BrightCart reporting P95 jump at ~07:55 PT. Asha attached sample request IDs.

Initial ask: we need a triage owner (SRE), a short customer note, and a product decision on whether to enable a temporary routing exception (route BrightCart to lower-quant model variant / lower batch targets) while we investigate.

Immediate asks: 
- Ben: can SRE confirm whether the spike correlates with any kernel scheduling/queue depth changes?
- Karthik: if we need a temporary routing exception, what's the UX risk and how fast can we push one?
- Marissa: draft a short customer-facing note (1–2 lines + ETA) that I can send to Asha within 30m.

Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency spike this morning — urgent

Triage update (SRE):
- Observed an abrupt rise in request queue depth on gen-api frontend starting 07:54 PT. Kernel scheduling metrics show increased stall time on GPU host pool g3-2 between 07:55–08:05.
- Not correlated with autoscaler changes or capacity churn. No deploys during the window.
- Early sign: long-context requests (>= 2k tokens) showed disproportionate q-depth growth — looks like KV cache pressure + large prefix batching.

Immediate mitigations we can do in the next 30–45m:
1) Apply per-tenant dynamic batch cap for BrightCart (limit simultaneous long-context batches to 2) — low-risk, instant config flip.
2) Temp route BrightCart to m-variant-qa (quantized variant, slightly lower quality for long contexts) — requires product approval, ~20–40m to push and validate fallback policies.
3) Evict stale KV-cache entries for a subset of hosts — SRE action, moderate risk, ~25m.

I recommend option 1 as fastest and reversible. I'll start the cap flip once Marissa has the customer note. Sending logs to the shared doc.

— Ben
Sr. SRE

Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Update: BrightCart latency spike & temporary mitigation

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the heads-up and the sample IDs — they were very helpful. Quick update: our SRE team has put a tenant-specific batch cap in place that will limit concurrent long-context batches for BrightCart. This is a reversible configuration change and should reduce P95 impact quickly. We expect observable improvement within 10–15 minutes.

We’re also planning a short fallback (route to quantized variant) as a secondary option if the cap doesn’t fully restore baseline. That would have a small quality tradeoff for very long contexts; we won’t enable it without your sign-off.

ETA: stabilization expected by ~09:25 PT; root-cause analysis and decision log to follow by 13:00 PT.

Attached: brief impact snapshot and SRE bridge logs.

If you want a call, I’m available at 09:30 PT.

— Naomi
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Decision log: routing exception evaluation and roadmap ask

Decision summary: 
- Action taken: Per-tenant dynamic batch cap (BrightCart) applied at 08:55 PT; P95 returned to baseline by 09:22 PT. No customer-visible quality change observed after cap.
- Secondary fallback (route to quantized variant) not enabled.
- Root cause (preliminary): burst of long-context requests exposed combined KV cache churn + large prefix batching sensitivity in current kernel scheduling for host pool g3-2.

Product/Roadmap asks (owner assignments):
1) Short-term: add a tenant-aware batching knob into routing policy so SREs can apply caps without product push (owner: Karthik) — ETA 3 sprints.
2) Medium-term: KV cache eviction heuristics improvement to avoid synchronized eviction across hosts (owner: Soojin) — ETA 6 sprints.
3) Longer-term: exploration ticket to evaluate kernel scheduling tweaks for long-context optimization (owner: Ben / Runtime) — FE: create RFC by 2027-05-10.

Customer comms: Naomi/Marissa to send a post-mortem summary by 13:00 PT with impact metrics and remediation timeline. Include the attached bridge logs and a link to the decision log.

— Karthik Iyer
VP, Product — Serving
Redwood Inference
